mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL growth reverts below 2% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE increases within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past 3 months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST growth reverts below 5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO growth rebounds within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or both PAYEMS and UNRATE revert to positive growth within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% during a recession signals a further contraction in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS growth rebounds within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening supply and monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or both INDPRO and FEDFUNDS revert to positive growth and decrease, respectively, within 3 months.
